newsitem.title: USA: Muni yield curve continues flattening -- Delphis.
newsitem.headline: Muni yield curve continues flattening -- Delphis.

text.p: The municipal yield curve flattened for the third week in a row in the week ended Thursday, Delphis Hanover Corp. said Friday.
The flattening came amid price gains for long-term bonds, while short-term prices held steady on the week.
The spread between one-year and 30-year bonds in the triple-A category narrowed 10 basis points to 175 basis points, after narrowing five basis points in each of the prior three weeks.
The Baa yield curve between one-year and thirty-year bonds flattened 15, to 175, after two consecutive weeks in which it flattened five basis points.
Average yields on one-year municipal bonds were unchanged across the credit spectrum for the second week in a row, holding at 3.90 percent in the triple-A category and 4.70 percent on Baa's.
The intermediate sector lost 10 basis points for the week, with yields on Aaa-rated 10-year bonds dropping to 5.05 percent and Baa-rated ten-years falling 10 to 5.90 percent.
Long-term municipals underperformed the Treasury market during the week.
The yield on the Treasury's 30-year bond fell 22 basis points to 6.91 percent by the close on Thursday, after rising six the week before.
Thirty-year municipal yields, meanwhile, fell 10 basis points to 5.65 percent in the triple-A category, after dropping five the week before.
Yields fell 15 basis points to 6.45 percent for 30-year Baa's after falling five the prior week.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis yielded 81.8 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday, compared to 81 percent the week before.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged for the third week in a row at 80 basis points. The 30-year spread narrowed five basis point to 80 basis points.
